author: leolara
content:
<@840207942581747712> I have been working FVd the specs, first with the consensus specs. The idea came from my time on the EF STEEL team. Repo: https://github.com/etheorem/etheorem (there are other 3 people contributing as of now)

<@543900561460822016> what you describe is what we have today, an executable Lean 4 port of the consensus specs that passes the official vectors:

- SSZ (SizzLean): full spec type set, 2188/2188 in-scope ssz_generic vectors
- Consensus specs for Fulu, Gloas and Heze: official consensus-spec-tests vectors pass at both presets, pinned v1.7.0-alpha.11
- Proofs so far: 3 of 5 planned SSZ properties, roundtrip, injectivity, size bound, over 13 constructor arms. On consensus specs 8 of 585 spec functions characterized, 29 more touched
- Trust base: 3 named SHA-256 equivalence axioms, and #print axioms prints everything a theorem uses

<@755590043632140352> I agree, conformance alone is not FV of the protocol. The invariants you list, slashable stake on contending finalized branches, strictly increasing justification, are the level above, and we are not there yet. What we have now is the base: the spec runs, and the first functions have characterization proofs.

On the black box worry: this one runs and passes the pyspec vectors, so implementers can execute it and compare. And where the Lean4 spec and pyspec disagree, we record it, and a human decides which one is right, same as @Micah says.

@TauLepton on AI proofs, honestly I don't understand the proofs in detail, but they are machine checked, so I know the theorem is proven. What we humans review is the proposition.

<@602753420033785856> interesting that you use Aeneas. We are studying a translator from the Python specs to Lean 4 in that spirit, it would keep the port in sync with pyspec automatically.

author: leolara
content:
And the test vector point of <@543900561460822016> is the next step we are working on. The category-partition method from a note I wrote on the STEEL blog, https://steel.ethereum.foundation/blog/2026-06-11_specs-as-models/, can run in Lean 4 directly: the spec is the model, and the test vectors would generate automatically for all clients. This Is how I think FV can help the clients, not by verifying them formally, but by generating tests vectors automatically from a model that is formally verified.

I will copy a summary of this to the ethresear.ch thread too, as <@840207942581747712> asked.
